title: Critères de Wells pour la TVP
short_title: Score de Wells pour la TVP (thrombose veineuse profonde)
formula:
Addition des points sélectionnés :

| Variable | Points | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cancer actif (traitement ou soins palliatifs dans les 6 mois) | Non | 0 |
| Oui | 1 | |
| Alitement récent >3 jours ou chirurgie majeure dans les 12 semaines | Non | 0 |
| Oui | 1 | |
| Œdème du mollet >3 cm par rapport à l'autre jambe (mesuré 10 cm sous la tubérosité tibiale) | Non | 1 |
| Oui | 1 | |
| Veines superficielles collatérales (non variqueuses) présentes | Non | 0 |
| Oui | 1 | |
| Œdème de toute la jambe | Non | 0 |
| Oui | 1 | |
| Sensibilité localisée le long du système veineux profond | Non | 0 |
| Oui | 1 | |
| Œdème prenant le godet, limité à la jambe symptomatique | Non | 0 |
| Oui | 1 | |
| Paralysie, parésie ou immobilisation plâtrée récente du membre inférieur | Non | 0 |
| Oui | 1 | |
| TVP documentée antérieurement | Non | 0 |
| Oui | 1 | |
| Diagnostic alternatif à la TVP aussi probable ou plus probable | Non | 0 |
| Oui | -2 | |

Remarque : il existe plusieurs versions des critères, avec des différences mineures selon l'étude ; cet ensemble est le plus largement validé, d'après [Wells 2003](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/14507948).

how_to_use.why:
- L'évaluation traditionnelle de la TVP conduit souvent à une imagerie par échographie (US) chez de nombreux patients, avec le temps et le coût associés.
- Ces critères aident à identifier les patients chez qui une TVP est peu probable et qui peuvent poursuivre par un dosage des D-dimères, permettant potentiellement d'éviter l'US lorsque les D-dimères sont négatifs.
how_to_use.when: Use in the outpatient and emergency department setting to estimate the pretest probability of deep vein thrombosis (DVT).
how_to_use.pearls:
- Patients with low clinical suspicion (<25% pretest probability) have a low prevalence of DVT.
- A score ≤1 (“DVT unlikely”) combined with a negative D-dimer can safely exclude DVT in up to ~30% of patients, with <1% subsequently diagnosed with VTE during follow-up.
- The score incorporates clinical judgment via the −2 point adjustment when an alternative diagnosis is at least as likely as DVT.
- Sequelae from DVT include pulmonary embolism (PE) and pulmonary hypertension, which have an associated mortality of 1%–8%
- May be less useful in hospitalized patients ([Silveira et al., 2015](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/25985219)) and/or patients with cancer ([Geersing et al., 2014](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24615063)).
- Validated internationally, but data across race and ethnicity remain more limited despite known ethnic differences in VTE prevalence.
- Intended to guide diagnostic next steps rather than to establish a diagnosis on its own.

next_steps.advice:
- As with all clinical decision aids, this tool is meant to support clinical decision-making, not dictate management.
- Apply these criteria only after a detailed history and physical examination is performed.
- Use only when DVT is being considered; if there is no clinical concern for DVT, risk stratification is unnecessary.
next_steps.critical_actions:
- Do not rely on the Wells’ Criteria alone to rule out DVT in high-risk patients or when clinical concern remains high.
- Evaluate for concurrent pulmonary embolism symptoms (e.g., chest pain, dyspnea) that may require urgent escalation in workup and management; decision aids, such as the [Wells’ Criteria for PE](nabda:calc.wells-criteria-pulmonary-embolism) or [PERC Rule](nabda:calc.perc-rule-pulmonary-embolism) , should be considered.
- Before starting anticoagulation, assess bleeding risk and contraindications; consider applying the [RIETE Score](nabda:calc.riete-score-risk-hemorrhage-pulmonary-embolism-treatment) .
next_steps.management:
Patients can be categorized as “DVT unlikely” and “DVT likely;” an additional “moderate risk” group can be added depending on the sensitivity of the D-dimer being used.

**Score ≤0:**

- DVT is unlikely (cited prevalence of 5%).
- Proceed to D-dimer testing.

 - A negative moderate- or high-sensitivity D-dimer reduces post-test probability to <1%; no further imaging is required.
 - A positive D-dimer should prompt US testing.

 - Negative US: Sufficient for DVT rule out.
 - Positive US: Consider anticoagulation for DVT.

**Score 1–2:**

- Moderate risk for DVT (pretest probability 17%).
- Proceed to **high-sensitivity D-dimer** testing (moderate-sensitivity assays are not sufficient).

 - Negative high-sensitivity D-dimer: Sufficiently rules out DVT (post-test probability <1%).
 - Positive high sensitivity D-dimer: Proceed to US testing.

 - Negative US: Sufficient for ruling out DVT.
 - Positive US: Consider anticoagulation for DVT.

**Score ≥3:**

- DVT is likely (pretest probability 17%–53%).
- Proceed directly to diagnostic US:

 - Positive US: Treat DVT.
 - Negative US: D-dimer testing can further risk-stratify patients.

 - Negative D-dimer:

 - DVT is sufficiently ruled out.
 - Consider discharge.
 - Positive D-dimer:

 - Still concerning for DVT.
 - Repeat US should be performed within 1 week for re-evaluation.

A note on US options:

- A negative **whole-leg US** (proximal + calf) usually rules out DVT without repeat imaging.
- A negative **proximal US** may require alternative imaging or repeat US in ~1 week if suspicion remains in moderate- to high-risk patients.

more_info:
Interpretation:

| Wells' Score | Risk group | Prevalence of DVT |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ≤0 | Low/unlikely | 5% |
| 1–2 | Moderate | 17% |
| ≥3 | High/likely | 17-53% |
